title: Guard block-rate = per-guard recurrence-prevention failure score (cost-weighted)
desc: Each guard's fire-rate (today vs 7-day average) is a per-guard recurrence-prevention failure score: it measures whether an embodied lesson is actually holding. Rising = the foundation is failing to catch the behavior at the door. Each block also costs a full-context server re-send, so the score is a hard cost metric.
steps: CONCEPT: a guard fire-rate -- today count vs trailing 7-day average -- IS a per-guard recurrence-prevention failure score. FLAT/low = the reflex/skill/push works (behavior stopped recurring). RISING (today much over 7d-avg, or trending up) = recurrence-prevention is FAILING there: the lesson was knowledge-ified but the embodiment is not catching it at the door.

ESCALATION (not re-warn): a rising score is PROOF the foundation is insufficient. Do NOT merely repeat the block -- STRENGTHEN the push: relocate the reflex onto the exact wire, harden the gate, or fix the root behavior. The loop: embody -> MEASURE (this score) -> if failing, re-embody stronger. This is how the harness self-audits whether it represents the user.

COST: each block forces a wasted tool round-trip that re-transmits the ENTIRE conversation context -- about one full-context cache re-send. So block-count is a hard COST/severity metric, and a longer session weights later blocks far heavier (a 200k-context block dwarfs ten 5k blocks). Recurrence-prevention is an ECONOMIC mandate, paid by every future session.

DESIGN (resolved): STORE per-guard daily COUNT (simple, deterministic, unbreakable, testable -- the maintainable core). DISPLAY a live cost proxy '~Xk ctx re-sent this block' from live session JSONL bytes / 4 (not stored, not summed, fails open to count). Full daily token-SUM is an OPTIONAL future enrichment. Implement centrally in Block/Emit (wkharness-common.ps1), one point, fail-open -- covers all guards.
author: claude
